chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: Friendship and open-door hospitality of audience fans
summary: He reflects that fans invited him into their homes, from Canada to Switzerland, with standing offers of rooms and insistence he visit.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Had you -- in your career as a musician had you ever run into this kind of friendly neighborliness before? Mostly, when you were working in clubs or hotels or something, I would think a kind of impersonal relationship. They'd come in. They know you there, but they don't know yououtside the club. Is it different here?

Well yes. Well yes and no, because I think that's an individual thing, because you meet people, and once you meet them, and they know you, then they'll come and invite you to their homes. I find you different, or you seem to be nice to know. Would you like to, or would you do us an honor to come to my home and meet my family. I think in -- it makes a gentleman, to meet my wife and daughters, and kids, or whatnot.
Wife, meet my -- you know, one of those things, come out to dinner one day, and then you go and you do that, and
this goes on. This goes on for years.
: I see.

Because once they know you, and you know them, they would introduce you to other very close friends of theirs, and it becomes a natural thing. You know. And it's doggone nice for a person, people come up, which I've met years ago, even before I met Fats, they come up to me and say well look, the next time you come this way remember, this is home. There will be a room waiting for you. And should you offer them pay for that, you would insult them.

You say you're one of us, so drop a card and let us know when you're coming this way, and your room will be ready. Oh, I know so many places where I could have done that, or I mean often has to do that. You know? Throughout years. And I think that's a heck of a thing.
: Did you usually --
Including Switzerland, by golly.
(Laughter.)
Right. I was talking about that. Did you often take up these offers and spend the --
Well, all --
: How did you feel about it?
Well you know, I mean you don't want to do that. I mean you come up, and you drop a card, or something, when they come -- what happened? Why didn't you

write us? Or why didn't you call? I say well, didn't you get my card? You know. You -- use the best bluff you can, oh, I didn't want to do it because I don't want to put you out. So now we're not going to take no for an answer. We will be insulted if you don't come out Sunday, one of those things. And oh, you just have to do it.
You have to drop all other commitments that you made, and you know.
So this was the -- this was the kind of atmosphere that you had in the Canadian-Vermont area.
Well, Canadian-Vermont area, and a lot of American --
Well, but I mean in a specific thing where you go in a hospital and people come to see you.
Oh, they -- oh, they were terrific. Those Canadians, I mean when you're going, and you come up, they say well you promised last time, remember? Remember?
(Laughter.)

Oh, man! And I've had people to get mad at me. Okay, we don't have a new car like such and such, but we doing-- I think we -- I says it's not a matter of that. So you have to trade -- get out of it the best way you can. You know?
